correctness.rationale: The stationary past stochastic integral exists in L2 by exponential decay of the Feynman–Kac semigroup; stationarity gives exact partial variances q1=D/k and q0=D/k+D/s. Conditional propagators obey a 2x2 linear system with eigenvalues -lambda_±, 0<lambda_-<lambda_+. The cancellation -(q1,q0)A/D=(0,1) proves -C'/D=phi_off, while R=(phi_on+phi_off)/2. Their difference solves a scalar stable second-order ODE with exact positive two-exponential solution, whose integral is 1/(2s), whose initial slope is k/2, and whose derivative has exactly one zero. The accompanying checker passed exact symbolic generators and 16 Taylor orders, 168 65-digit exponentiation comparisons, 14 sum-rule checks, 42 maximum checks and a rational instance. The proof, not numerical sampling, establishes universality.

value.rationale: Switched optical traps and noninstantaneous resetting motivate distinguishing thermal equilibrium response from stationary correlations. A universal strictly positive violation for each lag and an integrated anomaly exactly equal to half the mean switch-residence time provide nontrivial dynamical observables that previous stationary moment and entropy rates do not determine. The initial slope determines on-state stiffness and the unique peak determines the strongest lag-scale signal; the pair gives natural calibrated kinetic parameter reconstruction without access to full stationary density.
